title: midyear-ops-economics-and-reliability-sync-crestpoint-health
summary: Midyear operational and cost review focused on recent cost spikes, right-sizing dedicated capacity, and upcoming roadmap impact on reliability. Agreed to run a short perf/latency benchmark, share pricing scenarios for hybrid hosted/dedicated billing, and collect 7 days of production traffic for eval. Action items assigned for pricing, benchmarks, and security doc handoff.

Samir Patel: Draft perf benchmark plan + runbook and schedule test window (due: 2026-07-09)
Meera Singh: Provide 7-day production traffic sample and representative prompt set (due: 2026-06-30)
Jon Park: Share recent incident logs and percentiles for P95/P99 latency (due: 2026-06-29)
Karen Lo: Confirm procurement timeline and PO requirements (due: 2026-07-06)
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing scenarios and SOC2/KMS docs

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Alan Ruiz (CrestPoint CTO), Meera Singh (Head of ML), Jon Park (SRE), Karen Lo (Procurement)

Summary: Quick check-in on midyear numbers, unexpected cost rise in May, reliability incidents, and alignment on a small pilot for dedicated capacity right-sizing.

[00:00:00] Olivia (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Alan (CrestPoint): Alan here.
[00:00:10] Meera: Meera on the line.
[00:00:12] Jon: Jon, yep.
[00:00:14] Karen: Karen here.
[00:00:16] Samir (Redwood SE): Samir from the infra side.
[00:00:20] Olivia: Great. Agenda — we'll go through the cost anomaly, ops incidents, then get into options for right-sizing a dedicated pool and next steps. Sound good?
[00:00:35] Alan: Yep that's the plan. We want to understand why May jumped up and what to expect for Q3.
[00:00:45] Meera: Also want to know any accuracy regressions if we change quant or move models between hosted and dedicated. We run a triage for a release next month.
[00:01:20] Samir: Cool. Quick context from our side: when we look at your token distribution it's heavy tails — spikes during peak hours and some long-chat sessions that aren't batched well. That interacts with continuous batching and the KV cache, sometimes the cache (K-V cash in the transcript, ha) misses on long-tail prompts.
[00:02:05] Jon: We're seeing P95 latency creep up during the 10am PST window — coincided with the new feature launch. We pushed some retries which amplified token counts.
[00:02:45] Olivia: That matches the billing: burst tokens + retries. We flagged a few sessions with high generation depth. Karen, from procurement side, any constraints on moving to a dedicated commitment?
[00:03:10] Karen: Budget cycle is mid-July. We can sign a reserved month-to-month if the numbers look right, procurement needs PO terms and data residency assurances.
[00:03:40] Meera: Also security — can we get the KMS/HSM details and audit log retention? We need that for our compliance team.
[00:03:55] Olivia: Yes we'll share SOC 2 and KMS integration docs. We'll include log retention options in the pricing sheet.
[00:04:20] Samir: Operationally, one lever is smoothing requests into a dedicated pool with an autoscale bump for peak. Another is prefix/KV caching improvements and prompt engineering to reduce generation depth. We can also recommend quantization profiles for your model family to reduce GPU memory and cost — note that may slightly affect output quality.
[00:05:00] Meera: Hmm, quality sensitivity is high for our clinical triage flows. Any empirical numbers on quality delta for int8-ish quant?
[00:05:30] Samir: We have benchmark notes: for similar transformer families quant -> ~3-5% dropout on edge-case hallucinations but overall negligible in average token-level metrics. We'll attach the evals we ran; they're in the repo link we'll share. Might be mis-transcribed as 'repo lick' in the automated notes sometimes.
[00:06:10] Alan: Can we get a price comparison: pure hosted (pay-as-you-go) vs dedicated reserved with burst vs private on-prem? Lay out tradeoffs.
[00:06:30] Olivia: Absolutely. We'll produce three scenarios: 1) optimize hosted with caching + prompt fixes, 2) small dedicated pool sized to your P95 with autoscale for burst, 3) private deployment estimate. We'll call out unit economics (per-token and per-hour GPU) and break-even horizon.
[00:07:05] Jon: For the reliability incidents—we sent one incident report but want more granularity on the fallback behavior. When a region saturated, did Redwood fallback to another region or to a lower-cost model?
[00:07:30] Samir: Good question. For your tenant we had two fallbacks: first to a compatible model variant in the same region, then to a hosted lower-tier in a different region. You had a short window where KV cache warmed up poorly after failover which added ~120ms.
[00:08:00] Meera: That added jitter which affected our latency SLO for user-facing routing. Is there a way to pin model version across fallbacks to avoid cache cold starts?
[00:08:20] Samir: You can pin versions, yes. The tradeoff is capacity footprint and cost. We'll show a policy matrix in the runbook.
[00:08:50] Olivia: On the roadmap side, Redwood Optimize will be adding automated batch sizing suggestions and an eval guardrail to alert on prompt-set regressions. That should help your team detect cost vs quality changes earlier.
[00:09:20] Alan: When is that rolling out?
[00:09:30] Olivia: First tenant previews later July, GA in Q3 — we'll offer you early access if you want to run the evals.
[00:09:45] Meera: Yes please. We'd like to run it against our clinical prompt set.
[00:10:10] Jon: For benchmarks, we prefer a 2-hour window during a low-lift time but with a traffic replay to mimic peak. Can Redwood support a replay harness?
[00:10:30] Samir: Yes we can spin a replay harness. We'll need the traffic sample and anonymized prompts. Ideally a few different slices: short chit-chat, long session, and high-depth completions.
[00:11:05] Karen: For contracting, any minimum term for dedicated pools?
[00:11:20] Olivia: We usually offer monthly reserved capacity or 12-month commitments with discounting. We can show both in the pricing scenarios.
[00:11:50] Alan: Also curious about data residency — some of our records must stay in-country. Can you do region pinning for data plane?
[00:12:10] Samir: Yes, VPC/private deployments can be region-limited. For hosted, we offer region routing and we can restrict inference to specific regions for enterprise plans. We'll include options in the doc.
[00:12:45] Meera: A note on QA — we've seen minor regressions when moving from FP16 to some quant profiles. Would Redwood provide an automated eval against our golden set before we flip quantization?
[00:13:10] Samir: Yep that's part of the Optimize roadmap and something we can run as a one-off. We'll add it to the benchmark plan.
[00:13:45] Olivia: Ok let's pivot to the cost spike root cause. We analyzed billing and found three contributors: a) retries due to client-side timeouts, b) a new campaign that increased long-context sessions, c) an extra dev environment hitting prod tokens.
[00:14:15] Jon: The retries were from a faulty backoff in our client lib — we've patched it, should reduce the tokens by ~12% in July.
[00:14:40] Meera: The campaign is expected to continue for another 3 weeks but we can throttle depth on non-critical flows.
[00:14:55] Olivia: Great. That plus caching should close most of the gap. We'll model a conservative and aggressive savings scenario.
[00:15:30] Alan: On the reliability SLOs — what's Redwood's typical target for P95 and P99 with Dedicated?
[00:15:50] Samir: With Dedicated we aim for P95 under 300ms for small-to-medium context lengths, P99 under 900ms; your workload with long contexts will be higher. Our SLAs for enterprise can be tuned in contracts.
[00:16:10] Meera: Are outage credits in place for failovers?
[00:16:20] Olivia: Yes, we have crediting for downtime beyond SLA thresholds. We'll include the SLA table.
[00:16:40] Karen: Is there a standard SOC/ISO attestation package we can send to our legal?
[00:16:50] Olivia: We'll send SOC 2 Type II, ISO summary, and the KMS integration guide. I'll attach them to the follow-up email.
[00:17:20] Jon: For the perf tests, can we schedule next Tuesday window?
[00:17:30] Samir: I have availability Tuesday morning PST. We'll coordinate offline.
[00:17:45] Meera: Quick clarifying Q on model variants: if we fallback to a smaller variant, do you preserve the same tokenizer and decoding settings to keep output stable?
[00:18:00] Samir: We aim to keep tokenizer settings stable; decoding temperature/penalty defaults can be preserved but smaller models will behave differently. We'll document expected delta per variant in the plan.
[00:18:30] Alan: Any immediate things we can toggle today to avoid another billing surprise next month?
[00:18:45] Olivia: Short term: 1) reduce client retries, 2) set a hard max generation depth on non-critical flows, 3) enable prefix caching on common prompts. We'll send step-by-step for these.
[00:19:10] Karen: Procurement needs a sample contract with termination and data handling clauses; can you send a draft?
[00:19:25] Olivia: Yes, we'll include a redline-friendly sample.
[00:19:50] Meera: One more ops note — can we get token-level visibility in the console for the next 14 days? We need to pinpoint exact sessions.
[00:20:05] Samir: We'll grant a token-level dashboard export for your admin users for 14 days.
[00:20:40] Olivia: Alright let's capture decisions: we'll run a benchmark, CrestPoint provides traffic, Redwood sends pricing and docs, and both sides align on a procurement timeline.
[00:21:00] Alan: Sounds good. Thanks.
[00:21:15] Karen: Thank you.
[00:21:20] Meera: Thanks.
[00:21:30] Olivia: We'll follow up with an email that has the attachments and the proposed benchmark windows.
[00:21:40] Samir: I'll share the perf runbook and the replay harness steps.
[00:22:00] -- End of substantive discussion, remainder was scheduling and clarifications.
[00:27:30] (short silence and background noise)
[00:32:10] (speaker overlap) Alan: just to add — if we go dedicated do you support burst credits to absorb irregular spikes?
[00:32:35] Samir: Yes we have burst capacity and can set policies (cost-first vs latency-first) per route.
[00:36:05] Olivia: We'll model both cost-first and latency-first policies in the pricing workbook.
[00:41:20] Meera: Any gotchas switching region pinning later?
[00:41:40] Samir: There is some migration work to move KV cache snapshots across regions; it's doable but there is warm-up time. We'll document the migration steps.
[00:46:00] Jon: We'll aim to get the traffic sample up by 6/30.
[00:46:20] Karen: Procurement will reconvene after you send contract language.
[00:50:00] Olivia: Thanks everyone — we'll send the follow up items by end of day tomorrow.
[00:57:30] Meeting end.
